Another fun training day with my daughter, Lucy! Lucy woke up and asked if I could run her through a workout so of course we hit it.  As a 9 year old, we do a vast mix of training, but this training can be applied to any age (with modifications, of course): Cone game - lateral movement focus. This is a game the kids love and it’s a great warm up. Stand there and throw some cones back and forth while they try to “knock as many as they can” down. They don’t realize the reaction and lateral movement they are creating by simply playing a game!  Sandbag drags (or sled drag) is great for any age. Great from the ground up. If you suffer from knee pain, I highly suggest reverse sledding or reverse treadmill.  Dead hangs.  Amazing for grip strength, spinal decompression, shoulder mobility, back, core. Studies show grip strength is one of the strongest indicators of longevity.  Pushups. Lucy is killing it on the elevated pushups. This set she hit 13 with good form. We have moved her down every week and pretty soon she will be killing them from the floor.  Jumping. By far the best thing for children imo. Requires power and strength, coordination, and deceleration. Power is lost way before strength in adults. Somewhere along the lines adults stop jumping and creating true power and it’s a detriment to our capabilities.  Isometrics. Awesome for any age. Great for joint-angle specificity and muscle growth.  These workouts are not just for my 9 year old. Modifications can be made for any fitness level. Get out there and get after it today! 📚 Study to understand, not to cram. If you only memorize, you’ll forget after the exam. When you understand why something works, your brain remembers it longer and you can answer unfamiliar questions with confidence. 🔁 Use Active Recall instead of re-reading. After studying a topic, close your notes and try to explain everything you remember. Every time you struggle to recall something, your brain becomes stronger at retrieving that information. ⏳ Revise with Spaced Repetition. Don’t read a topic once and abandon it. Revise it after 1 day, 3 days, 7 days, and again later. This tells your brain the information is important and prevents forgetting. 🗣️ Teach the topic like you’re a lecturer. If you can’t explain it in simple words, you don’t understand it well enough. Teaching exposes the exact areas you need to work on. 📝 Practice with past questions early. Past questions reveal how lecturers think and the pattern of exams. They also train you to apply knowledge instead of just recognizing it in your notes. 🎯 Spend more time on your weak areas. Most students keep reading their favorite subjects because it feels comfortable. Top students improve faster because they deliberately fix their weakest topics first. 📵 Remove distractions while studying. Every notification breaks your concentration, and your brain needs several minutes to regain deep focus. One uninterrupted hour is more valuable than three distracted hours. ✍️ Create short summary notes. After every study session, write the key ideas on one page. During revision, you’ll review your summaries instead of hundreds of pages. 😴 Protect your sleep. Sleep is when your brain organizes and stores what you’ve learned. Reading all night and sleeping very little often leads to poor recall in the exam hall. 🚀 Be consistent, not extreme. You don’t need to study 12 hours in one day. Studying with focus for 2–3 hours consistently over weeks will outperform last-minute cramming almost every time. 🏆 Final Lesson: The smartest classmate isn’t always the one with the highest IQ. More often, it’s the one with the best study system, the most consistency, and the discipline to keep improving every single day. #studentmotivation #studytok #motivation #discipline #howtostudy

Na verdade, a divisão de treino é uma consequência da forma como distribuímos o volume semanal de treinamento. Portanto, o primeiro passo é definir o volume semanal que será destinado a cada grupamento muscular.
